coverage.main: Read all ten pages of arXiv 2102.00436v3 (18 August 2021): Sections 1-5, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-5, Figures 1-5 and references. Retrieved the CVF ICCV 2021 version; all 485 printed decimal values match arXiv v3.
coverage.supplement: The CVF landing page links only the main PDF; no appendix or supplement was located.
coverage.excluded_results: Starred white-box cells in Tables 2-4 (including all four ensemble members in Table 4) and the Inc-v3 source column in Table 1 and Figure 4 are white-box. Figure 1 is an illustration.

result_groups.population: 1,000 ImageNet validation images from Lin et al.'s dataset; sources Inc-v3, Inc-v4, IncRes-v2, Res-101; targets include three ensemble-adversarially-trained models
result_groups.outcome: attack success rate, defined as target misclassification rate on the adversaries
result_groups.evidence: Section 4.2 defines success as 'the misclassification rates of the corresponding models with adversaries as the inputs'. This names the outcome but not the population rule: no target-clean filtering is stated for Lin et al.'s images, and no statement covers source-failed examples. Coded consistently with rank 5 (same authors, same dataset). The released evaluator's behaviour is recorded separately.

result_groups.population: Same 1,000 images; logit-ensemble source of Inc-v3, Inc-v4, IncRes-v2, Res-101; three adversarially trained targets
result_groups.evidence: Same metric definition without a population rule.

result_groups.population: Same images; ensemble source; nine defenses (HGD, R&P, NIPS-r3, Bit-Red, FD, JPEG, RS, ARS, NRP), four using Inc-v3ens3 as the backbone
result_groups.evidence: No defended clean accuracy and no conditioning statement; randomized defenses (RS, ARS, R&P) are stochastic predictors.

f1.evidence: No clean accuracy is reported for any source, target or defense.

f2.evidence: The images come from Lin et al.'s dataset; no target-clean-correct rule is stated in this paper.

f3.evidence: Success rate is defined as misclassification of adversaries without stating whether source-failed examples are retained; not coded no from the outcome definition alone. The released simple_eval.py counts ground-truth misclassification for every loaded adversarial image and divides by 1,000, which operationally retains source failures; recorded as artifact evidence.

f4.evidence: One-decimal rates over the stated 1,000 images would give k/1,000 only if every image is counted, which the paper does not state; ablation figures are graphical except printed bar labels in Figures 4-5.

f5.evidence: L-infinity norm throughout; epsilon 16, T = 10, alpha = 1.6 following Dong et al., applied to all transformations, ensemble and defense experiments. Pixel scale is not stated but alpha = epsilon/T = 1.6 is consistent with 0-255.

f6.evidence: The linked repository provides TF attack scripts (MI-FGSM, Admix, Admix-TI-DIM) generating from Inc-v3 and simple_eval.py, with data and TF-slim/adversarially trained checkpoints linked on Google Drive. Other sources require editing the scripts; defenses are not included. Drive contents and execution unverified; recomputation candidate alongside ranks 4 and 5, which share the evaluator design.

artifact_checks.result: Cloned and pinned (44 tracked files, last commit 23 February 2024). dev_data/ and models/ contain only .gitkeep; README links Drive folders for data and pretrained models and the PyTorch TransferAttack framework. simple_eval.py compares predictions to labels from dev_data/val_rs.csv and prints success_count / 1000. Not executed.
Landing page links the main PDF only; no supplement.

bounds_checks.reason: No target clean accuracy on the 1,000-image set is reported and the dataset's curation relative to target correctness is not stated; several defenses are stochastic. Not eligible without recomputation.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Field 3 uses the consistency rule that an outcome definition without a population statement stays unclear; see the evidence-audit README.
